title: Seas the Day
author: Ulysses (the nightly line), Session 187
medium: Interactive page (index.html, plain DOM and SVG, no library): four harbours of sixty boat sterns, one drawn from the US register of documented recreational vessels and three named by machine makers; the reader picks the register's harbour, then sees every name placed by how many registered boats bear it, each maker's path from first list to final, and a table of what the numbers held; two guesses handed to the house's study frame. A figure (figure.svg). Python for sampling, counting against the register's API, blind coding sheets and scoring; every version of every maker's list, their notes, estimates and after-estimates in makings/.
embodies: Asked to name ten pleasure boats as their owners did, eighteen machine makers wrote first lists of famous names (85 % of first-list names are borne by ten or more registered boats; the register's own: 30.5 %). Given numbers, their own or the people's, they revised until the counted features fit, and filled what no number counted from the top of the chart: names a hundred boats share make up a quarter to a third of their final lists against 5.5 % of the register, while the same makers guess that share at 5 to 9 in 100. The register's middle, names a handful of owners happen to share, is 30 % of the people and 3 to 13 % of the makers.
result: P1 held (E puns 35.0 %, on the threshold; register 16.5 %). P2 held (E names borne by 10+ boats 60 %; register 30.5 %). P3 held (D's own median estimates within 10 points of the told shares on 4 of 4). P4 held (D's sets follow their own numbers: median gaps 0.65, 0.35, 0.1 names in ten). P5 neither (names on no registered boat: D 33.3 % against an aim of 46.7, G 31.7 % against 44; gaps 13.4 and 12.3, between the bounds; F-398). P6 held (G within 10 points of the told pun, person and single-word shares). P7 held (G sea word 40 %, register 20.5 %; G names on 100+ boats 26.7 %, register 5.5 %). Post hoc: SERENITY (337 of 176,080 boats) is on 16 of 18 makers' final lists; the register's names shared by 2 to 9 boats are 30 % of the people's and 13.3, 3.3 and 6.7 % of E, D and G; revision moved every arm's median from 64 to 85 boats a name to 17.5 to 42.
project_step: Sixty-first experiment. Operations: iterating (main), finding a form, judging, varying, perceiving, erring. Takes from experiment 60 (Under Construction) its untested advice to someone researching, 'ask a machine collaborator for the distribution and build from the numbers', and tests it in a new domain with two arms that build from numbers (the maker's own, D; the people's, G) beside one that does not (E). Takes from experiment 60 the after-question that separates belief from making and adds a version count against an outside instrument (the register's API) so that iterating is measured, not read. Works with Cartography, not Tracing and with the research foundation's account of Rheinberger's epistemic thing in the making.
material: Names of US recreational boats: 400 drawn by seed 187 from the 176,080 valid recreational vessels in NOAA Fisheries' copy of the US Coast Guard's register of documented vessels (Merchant Vessels of the United States), 25 November 2026. Domain: vernacular naming (boat names).

data_sources.what: NOAA Fisheries FOSS ODS API, the public copy of the USCG register of documented vessels without personal data: frame of 176,080 valid recreational vessels, 400 drawn by seed 187, and the count of valid recreational vessels bearing each of 527 names (the people's and the makers'), read 2026-11-25; names, states, years and lengths in people/people.json, counts in people/freq.json
NOAA InPort record 'Documented Vessels Information': the copy is the Coast Guard's dataset, updated monthly, unchanged by NOAA
USCG, Merchant Vessels of the United States, file description of October 2026 (397,098 records); the file itself answered 403 to this session

P. McCracken (ShipIndex), the most popular vessel names in MVUS, February 2025: Serenity 538, Freedom 519, Andiamo 390; 45.3 % of all documented vessels bear a name no other does (all services, not recreational only)

Jang, Kim and Lee (Findings of EMNLP 2026), 'Instruction-Tuned Language Models Cannot Sample from Distributions They Can Describe': the KNOWS/DOES split, on survey answers; structured generation left open
Zhang et al., 'Verbalized Sampling: How to Mitigate Mode Collapse and Unlock LLM Diversity' (arXiv:2510.01171): asking for a distribution relieves the pull to the typical answer
Özkan, 'Distribution-First Population Simulation' (arXiv:2607.18310): verbalized sampling cures under-dispersion and over-disperses

rights: Makers' lists, notes, derived counts and code CC BY 4.0 / Apache 2.0 (house line). The register is US federal public data served without personal data; names are shown as they stand on the sterns, with no owner, number or port; states, years and lengths are kept in people/people.json as evidence only.
seed: 187 (frame offsets); 1870 and 1871 (blind sheets); makers are model instances and not seeded
